subject: geography
title: Water Scarcity and Management
welcome_lead: Around 1.7 billion people lack safe water — explore why, and how to manage demand and supply.
meta_desc: IBDP Geography Adventure: water scarcity, transfers, dams and demand-side management.
final_note: You have weighed taps, dams and demand. The 21st century challenge is using water wisely.

concepts.def: Lack of water resources to meet demand, common in arid regions.
Inadequate investment in water infrastructure despite sufficient resources.
Per capita water availability below 1,700 m³/year.
Large-scale transport of water from surplus to deficit regions, e.g. South-North Water Transfer Project (China).
Reducing water use through pricing, efficiency, leakage repair and awareness.
Removal of salt from seawater or brackish water to produce freshwater, energy-intensive but expanding in the Gulf and elsewhere.

walkthroughs.body_html: The WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme estimates that approximately 1.7-2 billion people lack safely managed drinking water. Scarcity is uneven: Middle East and North Africa face acute physical scarcity, much of Sub-Saharan Africa faces economic scarcity. Population growth, urbanisation and climate change are intensifying pressure.

Dams (Aswan, Hoover, Three Gorges), inter-basin transfers (Tagus-Segura in Spain, South-North Water Transfer in China) and desalination (Saudi Arabia produces ~20% of world capacity) expand supply. Each carries social and ecological costs and high energy demand.

Cape Town's near-Day Zero crisis (2018) showed how rapid demand reduction is possible through tariff structures, leak repair and behaviour change. Drip irrigation, recycling of grey water and integrated water resource management (IWRM) are central to sustainable approaches. The SDGs target safe water and sanitation for all by 2030.
